title: Knowledge Graph Self-Supervised Rationalization for Recommendation

problem.claim: The method addresses identifying informative knowledge connections and rationalizing their effects in knowledge-aware recommender systems.

contributions.claim: KGRec is a self-supervised rationalization method for knowledge-aware recommender systems.
KGRec uses attentive rational scores for knowledge triplets and combines generative and contrastive self-supervised tasks through rational masking.
KGRec uses masking-reconstructing to highlight useful knowledge connections and contrastive learning to align knowledge and user-item interaction views while masking potentially noisy edges.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe KGRec as a new method and its masking-reconstructing task as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments on three real-world datasets demonstrate that KGRec outperforms state-of-the-art methods.
The authors provide implementation code for KGRec.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper introduces KGRec as a self-supervised rationalization method for knowledge-aware recommendation.
An attentive mechanism assigns rational scores to knowledge triplets.
Generative and contrastive tasks are integrated through rational masking.
The authors report improved performance over state-of-the-art methods on three real-world datasets.
